chunks: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Saʿd narrated from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام that he said:
"A man from my progeny will be killed unjustly by poison in the land of Khurāsān. His name will be my name, and his father's name will be the name of the son of ʿImrān, Mūsā عليه السلام.

Behold, whoever visits him in his estrangement, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will forgive his sins, those that have passed and those that come later, even if they are like the number of the stars, the drops of rain, and the leaves of the trees."

key_terms.النُّجُومِ: The stars; part of the comparison indicating immense quantity.
key_terms.الْأَمْطَارِ: The rains; another image for innumerable abundance.
key_terms.بِالسَّمِّ: By poison; the means of his unjust killing.
key_terms.خُرَاسَانَ: The land where the Imam from the progeny is foretold to be killed.
key_terms.ذُنُوبَهُ: His sins; the sins of the one who visits him.
key_terms.ظُلْمًا: Unjustly; indicating oppression in his martyrdom.
key_terms.غَفَرَ: He forgave; referring to Allah's forgiveness for the visitor.
key_terms.غُرْبَتِهِ: His estrangement; referring to his being far from his homeland and supporters.

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the Imam martyred in Khurāsān?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a prophecy from Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام concerning a descendant who would be martyred by poison in Khurāsān, identified by his and his father's names. It also describes the immense reward of visiting him in his estrangement, promising divine forgiveness for sins in abundance beyond measure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3188 - It is narrated from Nu‘man ibn Sa‘d, who reported that the Commander of the Faithful, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:
"A man from my progeny will be killed unjustly by poison in the land of Khurasan. His name will be my name, and his father's name will be the name of the son of Imran, Musa, peace be upon him.

Behold, whoever visits him in his estrangement, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Exalted, will forgive their sins—both past and future—even if they are as numerous as the stars in the sky, the raindrops, or the leaves of the trees."
